newsitem.title: PHILIPPINES: Uncertainties drag Manila shares down at close.
newsitem.headline: Uncertainties drag Manila shares down at close.

text.p: Philippine shares ended weaker on Monday after a firm opening, as uncertainties in the foreign exchange and money markets put investors on the defensive, brokers said.
"The drop in the peso caused the market to sputter a little bit," Irving Ackerman, president of Ackerman and Co, said.
The peso opened lower at 28.40 to the dollar, against Friday's close of 28, prompting the central bank to intervene.
A speculative attack on the Indonesian rupiah and Malaysian ringgit also raised the spectre of a similar attack on the peso, Ackerman added.
The composite index slipped 24.61 points, or 0.92 percent, to settle at 2,648.34.
The relatively high interest rates have likewise discouraged equity investments, Bing Trinidad, research head of DBS Securities, said.
The central bank did not cut its benchmark overnight rates after successively cutting it by a total of seven percentage points on Thursday and Friday.
The rate cut and a stabilising peso had propelled the key stock index by more than three percent late last week.
Blue chips led the decline on Monday. They included San Miguel Corp A and B and Ayala Land Inc .
San Miguel was being sold down on expectation of poor second quarter earnings due to lower sales volume.
Trinidad said the index is likely to trade between 2,600 to 2,800 in the coming days.
However, Ackerman said the market will still be dictated by the developments in the foreign exchange and money markets.
